lead: The racing rules are written in defined terms. Learn what keep clear, overlap, room and zone mean, and the right-of-way rules become short.

sections.title: Which side the wind is on
refs: RRS definition Leeward and Windward, RRS definition Tack, Starboard or Port
RRS definition Leeward and Windward, RRS 11
RRS definition Tack, Starboard or Port
RRS definition Tack, Starboard or Port, RRS 13
RRS definition Tack, Starboard or Port, RRS definition Leeward and Windward
RRS definition Tack, Starboard or Port, RRS 10
RRS definition Tack, Starboard or Port, RRS 11

blocks.p: Your **leeward side** is the side away from the wind. Head to wind, it is the side that was leeward before; dead downwind or by the lee, the side your mainsail lies on. The other side is windward, and it names your **tack**: starboard or port.

fig.note: The tack is the windward side, opposite the mainsail

blocks.p: So the tack changes only when you pass head to wind or, on a run, when the mainsail crosses. Of two overlapped boats on one tack, the one to leeward of the other is the **leeward boat**.

blocks.rule: Boom to port on a run: starboard tack.

sections.title: Behind you or alongside you
refs: RRS definition Clear Astern and Clear Ahead; Overlap
RRS definition Clear Astern and Clear Ahead; Overlap, RRS 11
RRS definition Clear Astern and Clear Ahead; Overlap, RRS 10
RRS definition Clear Astern and Clear Ahead; Overlap, RRS 18.2
RRS definition Clear Astern and Clear Ahead; Overlap, RRS 12

blocks.p: Take a line abeam from the aftermost point of your hull and equipment in normal position. A boat entirely behind it is **clear astern**; if neither boat is clear astern of the other, you **overlap**. Equipment counts: a rudder, a bowsprit set with its sail.

fig.note: B is clear astern of A · C overlaps A

blocks.p: Distance does not matter, and two boats also overlap when one between them overlaps both. On opposite tacks the terms apply only when both boats sail more than 90° from the true wind or when rule 18 applies between them; on a beat, rule 10 alone decides.

sections.title: Three yardsticks
refs: RRS definition Room, RRS definition Mark-Room

blocks.p: You **keep clear** when the right-of-way boat can sail her course with no need to take avoiding action and, if you are overlapped, can also change course either way without immediate contact. The test is her need to act, not distance or a hail.
**Room** is the space a boat needs in the existing conditions to manoeuvre promptly in a seamanlike way, including space to meet her obligations under Part 2 and rule 31.
**Proper course** is the course you would sail to finish soonest in the absence of the other boat the rule refers to. It shifts with the wind, and before your starting signal you have none.

sections.title: The words of a rounding
refs: RRS definition Zone, RRS definition Mark
RRS definition Mark, RRS definition Obstruction

blocks.p: A **mark** is an object the sailing instructions require you to leave on a stated side, or a committee vessel from which the starting or finishing line extends. A fender hung on it is part of it; its anchor line is not.

fig.note: Three hull lengths of the boat nearer the mark

blocks.p: The **zone** reaches three hull lengths of the boat nearer the mark. You are in it once any part of your hull is. Each gate mark has its own.

**Mark-room** is room to sail to the mark, round it on the required side and leave it astern: a seamanlike rounding, and room, not right of way. It includes room to tack only for a boat overlapped inside and to windward who would then be **fetching** the mark: passing to windward of it without another tack.

sections.title: What you cannot simply sail past
refs: RRS definition Obstruction, RRS definition Mark
RRS definition Continuing Obstruction, RRS definition Obstruction

blocks.p: An **obstruction** is an object you could not pass without changing course substantially if you sailed straight at it from one hull length away, or an area the event's rules close to boats. A boat racing is one only to boats that must keep clear of her or, under rule 22, avoid her.

tiles.name: Obstruction
tiles.note: one length away, straight at it

tiles.name: Continuing obstruction
tiles.note: three lengths or more along it

blocks.p: A **continuing obstruction** is one the boats pass along for at least three hull lengths; a vessel under way never is, nor a committee vessel that is also a mark. A small buoy is a mark without being an obstruction.

sections.title: When the race begins and ends
refs: RRS definition Racing, RRS Part 2 preamble
RRS definition Sail the Course, RRS 28

blocks.p: You are **racing** from your preparatory signal until you finish and clear the line and marks, retire, or a general recall, postponement or abandonment is signalled.

fig.note: At the signal: A is over and must come back, B may start

blocks.p: You **start** when, your hull having been entirely on the pre-start side at or after the starting signal, any part of it crosses the line. You **finish** when any part of your hull crosses the finishing line from the course side, unless you then take a penalty, correct an error in sailing the course or sail on.

To **sail the course**, your track drawn taut must pass each mark on its required side and each gate from the previous mark's direction. A mark that does not begin, bound or end your leg has no required side.

head: Signal
The race is
rows: Delayed; may be started or abandoned later

sections.title: What you agree to by racing

blocks.p: The basic principle: break a rule without being exonerated and you promptly take a penalty, perhaps retiring, whether or not anyone protests.

head: Rule
What it asks
rows: Help anyone in danger, racing or not; redress for places lost
Your flotation is your own responsibility
Fair sailing: a deliberate breach means a non-discardable disqualification
The decision to race is the boat's alone
Accept the rules and appeals; no courts

blocks.p: A **rule** includes the notice of race, sailing instructions and class rules, not club customs or the Basic Principles. A **protest** is an allegation under rule 60 that a boat broke a rule; the hail only announces it. Its **parties** are protestor and protestee, never witnesses or the protest committee.
